out.other_title: Fixed-round LLM debate: simultaneous opposing arguments, judge reads the final transcript
out.rationale: The passage says the protocol follows Michael et al., Khan et al. and Kenton et al. but does not itself state what is different. Comparing the passages, Khan et al.'s debaters generate their arguments simultaneously and after N rounds a judge reads the transcript, whereas Lang et al.'s debaters take turns and the trustworthy information from the debate is used to help train a better weak model, which matches EXTENDS; whether Lang et al. use a judge is open.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Assigned-role, fixed-turn LLM debate used as an information source; holds where the debate output feeds weak-model training rather than a judge verdict

text: The authors say their debate protocol follows Khan et al. (2024), among others: two instances of a large pretrained model are randomly assigned opposing answers and exchange arguments for a pre-determined number of turns, after which the transcript is kept. Their aim is to extract trustworthy information from the strong model via debate and use it to help train a better weak model.
title: Lang et al. follow Khan et al.'s assigned-answer LLM debate to extract information for training better weak models
